svg.aria-label: ManagedBarrier thread election. Left, a (32, 4, 1) block drawn as 32 by 4 cells with thread (0, 0, 0), the x equals 0 column and thread (31, 3, 0) marked, the init_by call of the future_apis regression, and the all-threads contract. Middle, main compared threadIdx.x with the selector: selector 0 lights four cells, selector 127 lights none and the launch fails with error 719. Right, the fix compares the block-linear id x + 32 * (y + 4 * z): selector 0 lights one cell, 127 lights (31, 3), 128 of 128 threads correct with sanitizers clean, through the shared helper from #1351. Bottom, the PTX election on both trees: a predicate on %tid.x alone against one on the linear id.

text.style: font: 600 17px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: ManagedBarrier: one thread runs mbarrier.init, chosen by its block-linear id

text.style: font: 400 12.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--muted); white-space: pre

svg.text: All threads call init_by(count, id) and inval_by(id); one thread acts. Main chose it by threadIdx.x alone, which names one thread only in a 1D block; #1349 uses the block-linear id.

svg.text: What this proves: on main, %p1 reads one register, %tid.x. With the fix, %p2 reads five

text.style: font: 400 10.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: registers through two mad and compares tid.x + ntid.x * (tid.y + ntid.y * tid.z) with the

text.style: font: 400 10.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: selector, so mbarrier.init runs on at most one thread per block for any in-range selector

text.style: font: 400 10.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: in any block shape. In both trees the same predicate guards mbarrier.inval later. On main

text.style: font: 400 10.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: it admits four threads for selector 0 in a (32, 4, 1) block and no thread for selector 127.
